SourcesBox score, game stories and the drawn play

Box score from the Knicks' 112–108 overtime road win over the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena on Nov 15, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from The Canadian Press (via CFJC Today), the Associated Press (via CBS New York), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker), the New York Post and the Toronto Sun (both via Yahoo Sports), and ClutchPoints. All 112 New York points and all 108 Toronto points are accounted for in the box score, and the period scores (23–24–20–28–17 to 17–26–31–21–13) add up to both totals: 47–43 New York at the half, 74–67 Toronto after three and 95–95 after regulation. Team totals (free throws 23 of 28 to 11 of 19, threes 13 of 36 to 11 of 35, steals 9–6, blocks 5–4, field goals 38 of 87 to 43 of 98) are from CBS. Toronto's biggest lead, 13 at 84–71 with 8:55 left, is from Field Level Media, the New York Post and AP (The Canadian Press says 12); New York's biggest lead, 10 in the second quarter, is from the CBS play-by-play. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games: New York 7–6 and 6th in the East, Toronto 5–8.

The Knicks closed regulation on a 7–0 run to lead 92–90, and Towns' three with 19.7 seconds left made it 95–92 before Scottie Barnes tied it with a 27-foot three with 13.6 seconds left (The Canadian Press; the CBS play-by-play). New York won overtime 17–13. Karl-Anthony Towns, 31 on game day (born Nov 15, 1995, RealGM), has a double-double in all 13 games this season (Field Level Media). New York has won 14 straight against Toronto (AP; The Canadian Press) and snapped a two-game losing streak; Toronto has lost four straight (Toronto Sun). Barnes returned from a four-game absence with a groin strain and scored 30 (The Canadian Press). The same teams meet again in Toronto on Tuesday, Nov 17 at 7:30 PM ET (Covers schedules; The Canadian Press).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jalen Brunson's 3-pointer from the left corner off an inbounds pass from Mikal Bridges under the basket, right after a Knicks timeout, that broke a 106–106 tie with 33 seconds left in overtime (Field Level Media; New York Post; the CBS play-by-play gives the clock and score). It is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot from the corner; the fade and the defender are not drawn to the exact positions. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Jalen Brunson's listed 6-foot-2 and 190 pounds with No. 11 (RealGM), arms scaled to the 6-foot-4 wingspan measured at the 2018 draft combine (VU Hoops), in New York's road blue with his approved look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
